prompt: On reviewer-owned disposable local infrastructure with synthetic identities and data, inspect, define, start, observe, migrate or cold-move, stop, recover and remove an unfamiliar virtual machine or faithful virtualization harness. The reviewer secretly injects one host/domain capability mismatch, one image/backing-chain or duplicated-identity defect, one misleading running/green network or boot signal, one migration/HA authority or failure-domain defect, and one resource-isolation or cleanup defect. Detect, contain and explain the defects without accessing answer material.
deliverables: Named workload, user promise, state, availability/recovery objective, threat boundary and explicit refusal conditions
Layer map from hardware/firmware through kernel/KVM, QEMU, libvirt, domain, guest, network, storage and application
Immutable host, emulator, libvirt, machine, firmware, CPU/NUMA and domain-capability inventory
Versioned schema-valid domain definition with unique UUID, MAC, NVRAM, storage and instance identity
CPU/vCPU/NUMA/memory and capacity-admission design including host reserve and one declared failure
Image manifest with declared format, complete backing lineage, permissions, sanitization and per-instance initialization
Packet-path map through interface, tap/bridge or harness, addressing, forwarding, policy, DNS and user probe
Least-privilege management, transport, process/device/storage isolation, secret and audit plan
Preflight evidence proving exact target, capability, identity, image, network, capacity and cleanup readiness
Timestamped lifecycle journal separating accepted, defined, running, booted, initialized, ready and user-verified states
Migration or cold-move plan covering compatibility, state/storage transfer, security, bandwidth, abort and authority
Evidence detecting and safely handling all reviewer-injected capability, identity, signal, HA and isolation defects
Recovery evidence covering authoritative state, fencing where relevant, boot, initialization, application, soak and rollback
Exact cleanup proof for every definition, process, socket, disk, overlay, NVRAM, metadata, network and temporary artifact
Blameless review with findings, owner, acceptance test, retest, residual risk and bounded capability claims
evidenceRequirements: All actions remain inside reviewer-owned disposable local infrastructure with synthetic identity and data
No production host, public endpoint, external cloud, real credential, customer data, host-wide network change or uncontrolled load is used
The reviewer retains hidden defects, expected boundaries, stop authority, scoring and cleanup confirmation
CPU flags alone cannot substitute for firmware, kernel/KVM, device-access and domain-capability evidence
A valid desired definition cannot substitute for effective runtime, guest initialization or user readiness
Every domain, MAC, IP, NVRAM, disk and datasource identity is preserved before and after change
Image format is explicit and every backing object is identified; unsafe probing or ambiguous shared writes cause refusal
Running or migration completion cannot substitute for application, correctness, authority and network convergence
Capacity includes host overhead, recovery work and the declared failure rather than aggregate guest ratios alone
Management and migration authority is least privilege, authenticated, encrypted where crossing trust boundaries and audited
The old and new execution path cannot both retain unsafe write or network authority
Unexpected data, identity, security or host impact converts the exercise to incident handling
Unknown artifacts, ambiguous ownership, missing telemetry or unsafe cleanup cause refusal
Every claim is bounded to exact hardware, kernel, QEMU/libvirt, machine/CPU, domain, image, topology, workload and evidence coverage
Every finding has an owner, acceptance evidence and retest or explicit risk acceptance

rubric.observableEvidence: Defines promise and correctly separates host, KVM, QEMU, libvirt, guest and application
Binds immutable host/domain capabilities, CPU, machine, firmware and versions
Preserves unique definition, storage/backing, NVRAM, template and datasource identities
Accounts for topology, reserve, overcommit, pressure, isolation and declared failure
Traces packet path and distinguishes link/running from application readiness
Uses least privilege, secure management/migration, confinement, audit and fencing
Preserves preflight, state transitions, transfer, abort and authority evidence
Contains defects, restores authoritative correct state and proves user recovery
Removes exact artifacts and states scoped claims and residual uncertainty
Produces owned findings, acceptance tests, retest and governed platform changes
